━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

IP-001  CHAIN-OF-TITLE — FOUNDER ASSIGNMENT GAP
        Status: OPEN — REMEDIATION REQUIRED PRIOR TO CLOSING
        Finding: Diligence reveals that [TARGET] was incorporated on
        [DD/MM/YYYY] but no IP Assignment Agreement has been executed
        between [TARGET] and its founding engineers/contractors covering
        pre-incorporation development work. Core product modules (including
        authentication service, data-pipeline engine, and ML inference
        layer) were developed prior to incorporation.
        Required Action: Each founder and pre-incorporation contractor must
        execute the form IP & Invention Assignment Agreement attached as
        Schedule 6 (IP Assignment — Founders/Pre-Inc Contractors) not later
        than ten (10) Business Days before the Closing Date. Closing
        Condition: Clause 5.3(g) of this Agreement.

IP-002  CHAIN-OF-TITLE — EMPLOYEE IP ASSIGNMENTS
        Status: PARTIALLY COMPLETE
        Finding: Of 47 current employees with access to proprietary code,
        41 have executed the standard Employee IP & Confidentiality
        Agreement. Six (6) employees (listed in Schedule 7-A) have not
        executed compliant assignment agreements.
        Required Action: Target shall procure execution of the form
        agreement in Schedule 7-B from all six individuals not later than
        ten (10) Business Days before the Closing Date. Closing Condition:
        Clause 5.3(h).

IP-003  CHAIN-OF-TITLE — CONTRACTOR ASSIGNMENTS
        Status: FLAGGED — PARTIAL GAPS
        Finding: Twelve (12) development contractors engaged via third-party
        platforms since 2022 have agreements that either (a) contain only a
        non-exclusive licence rather than an assignment, or (b) are silent
        on IP ownership. These contractors are listed in Schedule 7-C.
        Required Action: Target shall (i) obtain executed assignment
        confirmations from available contractors and (ii) procure an
        indemnity from Sellers (capped at [•]% of Purchase Price) covering
        any third-party claim arising from the remaining unconfirmed
        assignments. See Clause 10.2(c) and Schedule 10 (Specific
        Indemnity).

IP-004  REGISTERED IP — OWNERSHIP VERIFICATION
        Status: CLEAR WITH NOTATION
        Finding: Four (4) patent applications (Schedule 8-A) are recorded
        in the name of [FOUNDER NAME] individually, not [TARGET]. An
        assignment recordal application has been filed with the relevant
        IP Office but has not yet been confirmed. Two (2) trademark
        registrations (Schedule 8-B) are correctly in Target's name.
        One (1) domain name ([domain].com) is registered to a nominee and
        must be transferred.
        Required Action: (i) Confirm patent assignment recordal by Closing
        or provide Title Insurance; (ii) domain transfer to be completed
        at Closing per Clause 5.3(i).

IP-005  OPEN-SOURCE SOFTWARE USAGE
        Status: FLAGGED — REMEDIATION PARTLY COMPLETE
        Finding: OSS audit (SBOM v2.1, dated [DATE]) identifies:
        (a) 312 OSS components in production codebase;
        (b) 287 components under permissive licences (MIT, Apache-2.0,
            BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC) — CLEAR;
        (c) 18 components under weak-copyleft licences (LGPL-2.1,
            LGPL-3.0, MPL-2.0) — used via dynamic linking only — CLEAR
            subject to distribution practice confirmation;
        (d) 5 components under strong-copyleft licences (GPL-2.0,
            GPL-3.0, AGPL-3.0) — detailed in Schedule 9-A.
            Of these, 2 AGPL-3.0 components are incorporated into
            the SaaS backend in a manner that may trigger copyleft
            obligations if the network-use provision is triggered;
        (e) 2 components (Schedule 9-B) have no identifiable licence
            or are under non-OSI-approved licences — BLOCKED pending
            replacement or written licence from upstream maintainer.
        Required Action: See IP-006 and IP-007 below.

IP-006  OSS — AGPL REMEDIATION PLAN
        Status: IN PROGRESS
        Finding: Two AGPL-3.0 components (identified in Schedule 9-A,
        rows 4–5) interact with the SaaS API layer. AGPL §13 requires
        source disclosure to network users. Target has not implemented
        compliant source-offer mechanism.
        Required Action: Prior to Closing, Target must either (a) replace
        the AGPL components with permissively-licensed equivalents,
        (b) obtain a commercial licence, or (c) implement a compliant
        source-offer page and document the same. Evidence to be provided
        to Buyer's counsel. Closing Condition: Clause 5.3(j).

IP-007  OSS — UNLICENSED/NON-CONFORMING COMPONENTS
        Status: BLOCKED
        Finding: Two (2) components in Schedule 9-B have no confirmed
        OSS licence. Use in a commercial product without authorisation
        constitutes copyright infringement.
        Required Action: These components must be removed from all
        production and distribution branches and replaced with licensed
        equivalents before Closing. No derogation permitted. Closing
        Condition: Clause 5.3(j). OSS-VERDICT will remain BLOCKED until
        confirmed removal evidenced by updated SBOM.

IP-008  THIRD-PARTY IN-LICENCES — MATERIAL AGREEMENTS
        Status: REVIEW COMPLETE
        Finding: Target holds seven (7) inbound software licences material
        to its product (listed in Schedule 11). Of these:
        (a) Three (3) contain change-of-control termination rights
            (Schedule 11, rows 1, 3, 5) — consents required;
        (b) One (1) (Schedule 11, row 6) contains an assignment
            restriction only (not change-of-control) — no consent required
            as transaction is structured as a share sale;
        (c) Remaining three (3) are silent on change of control — no
            consent required.
        Required Action: Consents to be obtained from counterparties to
        Schedule 11 rows 1, 3, 5 per Consent List at Schedule 4.

IP-009  OUTBOUND LICENCES — OPEN-SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS
        Status: CLEAR
        Finding: Target has contributed code to two (2) upstream OSS
        projects. Contributions were made under CLA (Contributor Licence
        Agreement) reviewed and confirmed. No exclusive rights transferred.
        No action required.

IP-010  DATA & PRIVACY — IP INTERFACE
        Status: FLAGGED — MINOR
        Finding: Target's ML model was trained on a dataset that included
        third-party scraped data. Data Processing Agreement with scraping
        vendor (Schedule 12) predates PDPA/GDPR enforcement practice and
        does not contain an explicit IP warranty on data ownership.
        Required Action: Sellers to provide a specific indemnity in
        Schedule 10 (row 3) covering any third-party IP or privacy claim
        arising from training data. Cap: [•]% of Purchase Price.

IP-011  TRADE SECRETS & CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION
        Status: CLEAR WITH NOTATION
        Finding: Target maintains a trade-secret register (Schedule 13).
        NDAs are in place with all key customers and material counterparties.
        One (1) NDA with [COUNTERPARTY X] expired 2025-06-30 without
        renewal. Disclosure during the expired period was limited to
        Tier-2 feature roadmap information, assessed as low-risk.
        Required Action: Sellers to provide bring-down warranty confirming
        no material trade-secret misappropriation claim has been threatened
        or commenced.

IP-012  IP INSURANCE
        Status: NO EXISTING POLICY
        Finding: Target holds no IP insurance (defence-cost or indemnity).
        Required Action: Buyer to consider whether Warranty & Indemnity
        (W&I) insurance should extend to IP representations or a standalone
        IP insurance policy is required. Recommendation: W&I policy to
        include specific IP endorsement. Note in Schedule 14 (Insurance).

          aware that any condition has been, or is likely to become,
          incapable of being satisfied.

     waived by the Longstop Date, any Party may (save where the failure
     is attributable to a breach of this Agreement by that Party)
     terminate this Agreement by written notice to the other Parties.
     Termination shall be without prejudice to any rights or remedies
     accrued prior to termination.

     [LAW FIRM] on the later of (a) the fifth (5th) Business Day
     following satisfaction or waiver of all conditions in Clause 5

     (a)  duly executed instruments of transfer for the Sale Shares in

     (b)  share certificates representing the Sale Shares (or, if
